chunks: Al-Sayyari from Ali ibn Asbat who said:

When Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) arrived before al-Mahdi, he found him returning the wronged (restoring rights). He said to him, 'What is the matter with our injustice, O Commander of the Faithful? You do not return it.' He said to him, 'And what is it, O Abu al-Hasan?'

'Indeed, when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, opened for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) Fadak and what was attached to it, and there was no marching of cavalry or riding beasts upon it, Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'And give to the near of kin his right.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not know who they were, so he consulted Gabriel (peace be upon him) about that and asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about it. So Allah revealed to him, 'Give Fadak to Fatimah (peace be upon her).'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called her and said to her, 'O Fatimah, indeed Allah the Exalted commanded me to give you Fadak.' She said, 'I have accepted, O Messenger of Allah, from Allah and from you.' So its trustees remained in it during the life of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

When Abu Bakr took charge, he removed its trustees from it. So she came to him and asked him to return it to her. He said to her, 'Bring me a black or a red one to testify to you about that.' So she came with the Commander of the Faithful, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and Umm Ayman, and they testified to her about that. So he wrote for her a deed of non-interference.

So she left with the document with her. Umar met her and said to her, 'What is this with you, O daughter of Muhammad?' She said, 'A document that Ibn Abi Quhafah wrote for me.' He said to her, 'Show it to me.' She refused, so he snatched it from her hand, looked at it, spat in it, erased it, tore it, and said, 'This is because your father did not march upon it with cavalry or riding beasts.' And he left it and went away.'
So al-Mahdi said to him, 'Flog her for me.' So he flogged her. He said, 'This is too much,' so he paused to consider it.

key_terms.أَسْوَدَ أَوْ أَحْمَرَ: A black or a red one (referring to a human witness)
key_terms.بِتَرْكِ التَّعَرُّض: Deed of non-interference/exemption from further claims
key_terms.فَدَك: Fadak (a fertile land/garden given as a gift to the Prophet)
key_terms.لَمْ يُوجَفْ عَلَيْهِ بِخَيْلٍ وَلَا رِك: Acquired without military effort/marching with cavalry or beasts

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia narrative regarding the ownership and loss of Fadak after the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia claim to Fadak as a divine endowment to Fatimah al-Zahra, rooted in the interpretation of 'Dhu al-Qurba' in Surah Al-Isra. It details the succession of custody from the Prophet to Abu Bakr, and the subsequent usurpation by Umar, who invalidated the deed by citing the 'no cavalry or beasts' clause, a narrative often used to underscore the legitimacy of the Ahl al-Bayt's material and spiritual inheritance.
